```plato
    //==
    // # Marching cubes — the cube kernel
    //
    // One cube's worth of work, written against two sampling functions rather
    // than against a grid type, so that the dense grids, the sampled SDF and a
    // procedural field all share exactly this code.
    //
    // Sign convention: the extracted region is where the sampled value is AT OR
    // ABOVE isoLevel, and configuration bit c is set when corner c is BELOW it —
    // Bourke's convention, which is what makes his table's winding come out
    // counter-clockwise seen from outside that region.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding, handedness, and normals.
    //
    // A field whose interior is the LOW side — every signed distance field, which
    // is negative inside — is marched by negating the sampled value, which the
    // SDF entry points below do.
    //
    // Corner samples are read again per cut edge rather than cached in an
    // eight-element array per cube. That is the cheaper trade at every grid size
    // worth marching: cut cubes are the surface, so their number grows as the
    // square of the resolution while the total grows as the cube, and the
    // overwhelming majority of cubes are uncut and pay only the eight reads the
    // configuration index needs. Caching would instead allocate on every cube,
    // including all of those.

    // The sampled value at corner `corner` of the cube whose minimum corner is
    // lattice node `cell`.
    MarchingCubesCornerValue(cell: IntegerVector3, corner: Integer, valueAt: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, Number>): Number
        => valueAt(
            cell.X + MarchingCubesCornerOffsetX(corner),
            cell.Y + MarchingCubesCornerOffsetY(corner),
            cell.Z + MarchingCubesCornerOffsetZ(corner));

    // The world position of corner `corner` of the cube whose minimum corner is
    // lattice node `cell`.
    MarchingCubesCornerPoint(cell: IntegerVector3, corner: Integer, pointAt: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, Point3D>): Point3D
        => pointAt(
            cell.X + MarchingCubesCornerOffsetX(corner),
            cell.Y + MarchingCubesCornerOffsetY(corner),
            cell.Z + MarchingCubesCornerOffsetZ(corner));

    // 1 when cube corner `corner` is below isoLevel — outside the extracted
    // region — and 0 when it is at or above it.
    MarchingCubesCornerBit(cell: IntegerVector3, corner: Integer, valueAt: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, Number>, isoLevel: Number): Integer
        => MarchingCubesCornerValue(cell, corner, valueAt) < isoLevel ? 1 : 0;

    // The configuration index of a cube: the eight corner bits, corner c in bit
    // c. 0 and 255 are the two uncut cases.
    MarchingCubesCase(cell: IntegerVector3, valueAt: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, Number>, isoLevel: Number): Integer
        => MarchingCubesCornerBit(cell, 0, valueAt, isoLevel)
         + MarchingCubesCornerBit(cell, 1, valueAt, isoLevel) * 2
         + MarchingCubesCornerBit(cell, 2, valueAt, isoLevel) * 4
         + MarchingCubesCornerBit(cell, 3, valueAt, isoLevel) * 8
         + MarchingCubesCornerBit(cell, 4, valueAt, isoLevel) * 16
         + MarchingCubesCornerBit(cell, 5, valueAt, isoLevel) * 32
         + MarchingCubesCornerBit(cell, 6, valueAt, isoLevel) * 64
         + MarchingCubesCornerBit(cell, 7, valueAt, isoLevel) * 128;

    // How many triangles the case table lists for configuration c: at most five,
    // found by the position of the terminating -1.
    MarchingCubesTriangleCount(table: Array<Integer>, c: Integer): Integer
        => table[c * 16] < 0 ? 0
         : (table[c * 16 + 3] < 0 ? 1
         : (table[c * 16 + 6] < 0 ? 2
         : (table[c * 16 + 9] < 0 ? 3
         : (table[c * 16 + 12] < 0 ? 4 : 5))));

    // Where the isosurface crosses cube edge e: the linear interpolation of the
    // edge's two corner positions at the parameter where the corner values reach
    // isoLevel. Equal corner values carry no crossing information, so they fall
    // back to the edge midpoint.
    MarchingCubesEdgePoint(edge: Integer, cell: IntegerVector3, valueAt: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, Number>, pointAt: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, Point3D>, isoLevel: Number)
        : Point3D
    {
        var a = MarchingCubesEdgeCornerA(edge);
        var b = MarchingCubesEdgeCornerB(edge);
        var va = MarchingCubesCornerValue(cell, a, valueAt);
        var vb = MarchingCubesCornerValue(cell, b, valueAt);
        var t = va == vb ? 0.5 : va.InverseLerp(vb, isoLevel);
        return MarchingCubesCornerPoint(cell, a, pointAt)
            .Lerp(MarchingCubesCornerPoint(cell, b, pointAt), t);
    }

    // The triangles of one cube, wound counter-clockwise seen from outside the
    // extracted region. Empty for the two uncut configurations.
    MarchingCubesCell(table: Array<Integer>, cell: IntegerVector3, valueAt: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, Number>, pointAt: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, Point3D>, isoLevel: Number)
        : Array<Triangle3D>
    {
        var c = MarchingCubesCase(cell, valueAt, isoLevel);
        var row = c * 16;
        return MarchingCubesTriangleCount(table, c).MapRange(t =>
            Triangle3D(
                MarchingCubesEdgePoint(table[row + t * 3], cell, valueAt, pointAt, isoLevel),
                MarchingCubesEdgePoint(table[row + t * 3 + 1], cell, valueAt, pointAt, isoLevel),
                MarchingCubesEdgePoint(table[row + t * 3 + 2], cell, valueAt, pointAt, isoLevel)));
    }

    //==
    // # Marching cubes — the lattice driver

    // The isosurface at isoLevel through a scalar lattice of nodeCounts sampled
    // nodes, as unwelded triangles. `valueAt` reports the sample at a node and
    // `pointAt` its world position; both are called only with in-range indices.
    // A lattice of n nodes on an axis marches n - 1 cubes, so an axis with fewer
    // than two nodes contributes nothing.
    //
    // The case table is read once here and passed into every cube.
    MarchingCubesLattice(nodeCounts: IntegerVector3, valueAt: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, Number>, pointAt: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, Point3D>, isoLevel: Number)
        : TriangleArray3D
    {
        var table = TriangleArray3D.MarchingCubesCaseTable;
        var columns = (nodeCounts.X - 1).Max(0);
        var rows = (nodeCounts.Y - 1).Max(0);
        var layers = (nodeCounts.Z - 1).Max(0);
        var plane = columns * rows;
        var cells = MapRange(plane * layers, n =>
            IntegerVector3(n % columns, (n / columns) % rows, n / plane));
        return TriangleArray3D(
            cells.FlatMap(cell => MarchingCubesCell(table, cell, valueAt, pointAt, isoLevel)));
    }

    //==
    // # Marching cubes — entry points
    //
    // The extracted region is always the AT-OR-ABOVE side of the iso level, and
    // faces wind counter-clockwise seen from outside it. The distance-valued
    // grids are negative inside, so they are marched on their negated values at
    // iso level zero, which puts their solid on that same side.
    //
    // Output is `TriangleArray3D`: unwelded triangles, each carrying its own
    // corners. Welding is a separate pass, and a caller who wants an indexed mesh
    // asks for `ToTriangleMesh`.

    // The isosurface at isoLevel through a dense scalar grid, bounding the region
    // where density is at or above isoLevel. Samples sit at CELL CENTERS, so a
    // grid of n cells along an axis marches n - 1 cubes and the extracted surface
    // spans the centers, not the full extent, of the grid.
    MarchingCubes(self: DensityGrid3D, isoLevel: Number): TriangleArray3D
        => MarchingCubesLattice(
            IntegerVector3(self.Values.ColumnCount, self.Values.RowCount, self.Values.LayerCount),
            (i, j, k) => self.Values.At(i, j, k),
            (i, j, k) => self.CellCenter(i, j, k),
            isoLevel);

    // The zero level set of a narrow-band distance grid: the surface of the solid
    // its negative cells describe. Cells beyond the narrow band hold
    // BackgroundDistance with the correct sign, so they contribute no crossing.
    MarchingCubes(self: LevelSetGrid3D): TriangleArray3D
        => MarchingCubesLattice(
            IntegerVector3(self.Distances.ColumnCount, self.Distances.RowCount, self.Distances.LayerCount),
            (i, j, k) => self.Distances.At(i, j, k).Negative,
            (i, j, k) => self.CellCenter(i, j, k),
            0.0);
```
